answer.rationale: Write-path p99 degradation during peak settlement with an irreversible release rules out rollback. Read-replica routing (b5) targets dashboard/read load, not the write path, so it likely won't help writes — verifying it to confirm scope. Regional failover (b2) fits regional degradation, not a capacity/peak pattern. Circuit breakers (b4) apply to a failing partner dependency, not indicated here. The strongest match is b3: provisioning headroom ahead of heavy write traffic absorbed a surge without customer impact. Adding capacity is reversible, preserves all writes, and doesn't touch the mandated security patch. Uncertainty remains about whether the new release increased write cost, so capacity is added as a guarded scaling step with close monitoring rather than a broad change.
